cons: Only plays into 2 team compositions, both limited in Support options. If you don't have either team, she has no flexibility to speak of;
Significantly more Signature weapon-dependent if used in Tune Strain mode; becomes a pretty recommended pick-up;
Uses 3 different Echo Sets in her 3 most important team options. Even her own flexibility is limited by needing multiple builds in each.
pros: Part of 2 of the best non-QuickSwap teams in the game and the best QuickSwap team in the game (plays into both Fusion Burst and Tune Strain);
Has lots of viable weapon alternatives in Fusion Burst mode;
Constant off-field grouping making single-target oriented DPSes excel in AoE scenarios;
Fast rotation, high damage, strong buffs and utility. Has all the markings of a top-tier secondary buffer/damage dealer.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Denia is a 5-star Fusion Rectifier Hybrid character who plays into the Fusion Burst and Tune Strain team archetypes. By either focusing on strong Fusion Burst application and related team-wide buffs, or an even stronger buffing profile for Tune Strain hypercarries depending on her mode, she deals a lot of damage, rotates quickly, and has a highly specialized but equally as powerful buffing profile, featuring constant off-field grouping as well for maximal performance in both AoE and single-target situations in the teams she plays in. Let's figure out how all of it works so we can squeeze the maximum performance out of her combat gameplay.

sections.heading: Resonance Mode explanation
paragraphs: Denia plays into either Tune Strain or Fusion Burst depending on her Resonance Mode (configurable at will before combat). They modify the following aspects of her kit:
Her "Etched Colors" Inherent Skill (can either increase party-wide Fusion DMG or Tune Break Boost);
Most of the attacks in her kit will either apply 1 stack of Fusion Burst or Tune Strain - Shifting and reset the duration of Tune Strain - Interfered;
In Tune Strain mode, she may fill each target's Tune Break gauge by 50% of the max once per enemy per battle;
Her Outro skill changes to either amplify party-wide Fusion Burst DMG or general DMG Amplification (15 to 40% depending on whether the buffed character can apply Tune Strain or not);
In Tune Strain mode, she obtains standard Tune Strain - Interfered response like Lynae, Mornye or Luuk.
Some Sequences are also impacted, but we will only cover her S0 kit here.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics, Rotation & Buffs
paragraphs: Other than her Resonance Mode, Denia's in-game combat focus will be on accessing her second Ultimate, "Final Act - Breakdown Form". Speaking of which, she has 2 forms she may switch between via her Ultimates: Stagecraft Form and Breakdown Form. In practice, Stagecraft Form only serves to fill the gauge Breakdown Form will utilize in order to increase the damage of attacks in that form as well as the speed at which she can access her Second Ultimate.

For this purpose, Denia has several Forte resources that we won't spend too much time detailing, as her standard rotations cover all of Denia's bases in both Resonance Modes and in both casual play and quickswap, so we will only focus on the moves her standard rotation will utilize, as follows;
Her Intro in Stagecraft Form refills a bit of "Void Particle" Forte gauge and Concerto; the same applies for her Stagecraft Form Skill and Basic 4 (accessed immediately after Intro);
She then consumes it via her Basic Attacks in Breakdown Form (after switching to it via her Ultimate) to access her 2 Skills;

Casting both Breakdown Form skills will allow her to perform her second Ultimate, placing an Erosion Field that constantly spins on the ground and applies Fusion Burst or Tune Strain while grouping enemies periodically, and she is then free to switch out.
The summary above essentially constitutes the main concepts of Denia's rotation that will grant the following buffs to the team:

Fusion Burst application (via a lot of her attacks and periodically off-field via her second Ultimate), constant off-field grouping (via second Ultimate), Fusion Burst DMG Amplification (via Outro) and Fusion DMG Bonus (via Echo Set and Inherent Skill) in Fusion Burst mode;

Tune Strain application and duration refresh (via a lot of her attacks and periodically off-field via her Second Ultimate), constant off-field grouping (via Second Ultimate), general DMG Amplification significantly increased if the target ally applies Tune Strain (via Outro) and Tune Break Boost (and some ATK% via Echo set effects and Inherent Skill).
Additionally, her Signature Weapon can also boost the ATK of the team if acquired!

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Denia has significant personal damage, a very specialized and equally capable buffing profile, and a fast rotation. All of these factors undeniably make her the prime Secondary choice for the teams that she plays in. However, this comes at a cost: specialization.

Denia is highly specialized towards Tune Strain and Fusion Burst teams, since most of her buffs are tailored to characters of only that archetype. While her personal DMG, general DMG Amplification capability on Outro (even if weakened) and her generalist buffs via Echo sets like Moonlit Clouds and her Signature weapon definitely exist and could make you think she has a strong general use case, she's nowhere near comparable to a proper generalist character like Lynae, or a less specialized support like Iuno for Heavy Attacks. This is her main (and realistically, only) flaw, aside from needing to change Echo sets in between each team, which can definitely cause build complications if you want to lean into her (albeit small) team flexibility.

As of her release, all Denia has access to is Fusion Burst teams with Aemeath and Tune Strain teams with Luuk Herssen, only giving her a total of 2 teams that she can play in with no certainty of additional teams coming in the future. However, the 2 teams that she does play in are stupidly strong in the current meta, work well in both single-target and AoE thanks to her, and overall, if you wish to have either DPS but they lack a proper premium team, and you wish to pick up a strong power upgrade to either your Aemeath or Luuk, Denia is the perfect opportunity to do this.

In conclusion, while Denia is un"denia"bly (I swear I'm funny) a highly specialized secondary buffer and damage dealer character, in the teams that she is specialized for, she's by all accounts ideal and will make your premium Fusion Burst and Tune Strain DPS characters unleash their full potential and be top tier provided you have the correct teammates to surround them.

synergies.commentary: Best and only DPS choice for Fusion Burst Denia, together with Aemeath they form one of the strongest teams in the entire game, excelling in both AoE and singletarget damage with a fast and easy rotation and a low reliance on Signature weapons to perform, with the only caveat being they're somewhat stranded for Supports with only Chisa and Lupa being able to draw out the team's full potential. Still, Aemeath is the main reason to be getting and using Denia and makes for a ridiculously strong team.

If Aemeath already has a strong team, but Luuk doesn't and needs a stronger fallback than Sanhua, then Denia in Tune Strain mode is his best in slot. Due to her capability to provide a stupidly strong general DMG Amplification to Luuk on her Outro, as well as ATK and Tune Break Boost buffs via her Signature and Echo set, and strong personal damage, all in a short amount of time with added constant off-field grouping to cover Luuk's AoE flaws, Denia is the ideal partner for him.

3rd slot options for Denia teams depending on what team she's ran in. Chisa is ideal with Aemeath but Lupa is an excellent fallback with alternative Echo set choices which will draw just about the same performance as Chisa. Mornye on the other hand is best for Luuk on Tune Strain Denia teams while providing nothing of value to Aemeath.
